items.title: qwen3-coder parser drops tool calls when model omits opening <tool_call> tag — tool call leaks into content as plain text
items.body:
### What is the issue?

When qwen3-coder:30b emits a tool call but omits the opening <tool_call> tag (a known flub of this model), Ollama's qwen3coder parser does not engage, and the entire tool call is returned as plain text in the message content. Agent clients (Claude Code in my case) therefore never execute the tool — to the user it looks like the model "lost" all its tools.

### Steps to reproduce

Run Claude Code against the Anthropic-compatible endpoint:
ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=http://localhost:11434, ANTHROPIC_MODEL=qwen3-coder:30b
Ask for any tool use, e.g. claude -p "Use the Glob tool with pattern *.md to list markdown files."
Frequently (not always) the response comes back as text instead of a tool_use block:

I'll use the Glob tool to list all markdown files in the current directory.

<function=Glob>
<parameter=pattern>
*.md
</parameter>
</function>
</tool_call>
Note the trailing </tool_call> with no opening tag — the model emitted everything except the opening trigger. The payload is unambiguous and fully recoverable; the parser just never engages.

### Expected behavior

The parser should fall back to recognizing a bare <function=...> block (with <parameter=...> children) in content and convert it to a structured tool call. Precedent: goose merged exactly this fallback for qwen3-coder output (block/goose#6883), and vLLM patches similar qwen3-coder tag edge cases (vllm-project/vllm#35615). This is the same bug class as #14745 and the qwen3.5 unclosed-think fix in #15022, but a different malformation that is not yet handled.

### Workaround

Appending a system prompt instructing the model to always begin tool calls with a literal <tool_call> tag restores tool calling, but it's probabilistic, not a fix.

### Environment

Ollama 0.30.7, Windows 11 Pro (10.0.26200), NVIDIA GPU (model runs 100% GPU)
Model: qwen3-coder:30b (id 06c1097efce0), 64K context
Client: Claude Code CLI v2.1.174 via the Anthropic-compatible API


### Relevant log output

```shell
**Server log** (`server.log`) — the request completes "successfully"; Ollama never detects the problem:


[GIN] 2026/06/12 - 14:05:16 | 200 |    7.8194183s |       127.0.0.1 | POST     "/v1/messages?beta=true"


**Raw `/v1/messages` API response** (captured via `claude -p ... --output-format stream-json`) — the
tool call comes back as a single `text` content block instead of a `tool_use` block. Note the trailing
`</tool_call>` with no opening tag:


{
  "id": "msg_f9dff4f012c93d80569635f8",
  "type": "message",
  "role": "assistant",
  "model": "qwen3-coder:30b",
  "content": [
    {
      "type": "text",
      "text": "I'll fetch the example.com webpage and report its title using the WebFetch tool.\n\n<function=WebFetch>\n<parameter=url>\nhttps://example.com\n</parameter>\n<parameter=prompt>\nWhat is the title of this webpage?\n</parameter>\n</function>\n</tool_call>"
    }
  ],
  "usage": { "input_tokens": 25977, "output_tokens": 0 }
}


Expected: `content` should contain a `tool_use` block with `name: "WebFetch"` and the parsed parameters.
```

### OS

Windows

### GPU

Nvidia

### CPU

AMD

### Ollama version

0.30.7

items.title: gemma4: tool calls using `key=value` instead of `key:value` fail to parse and return empty responses
items.body:
## What happens

gemma4 (tested: `gemma4:26b-a4b-it-q4_K_M`) sometimes emits tool-call arguments as
`save_as='report.docx'` or `save_as="report.docx"` instead of the canonical
`save_as:<|"|>report.docx<|"|>`. When it does, parsing fails and the API returns
**`tool_calls: []` with empty `content`** — the generated arguments survive only in the
server's warning log, so the client cannot recover or retry intelligently.

Server log:

```
gemma4 tool call parsing failed: invalid character 's' looking for beginning of object key string
repair failed to produce valid JSON arguments
```

## Why

`quoteGemma4BareKeys` (model/parsers/gemma4.go) only recognises a bare key when it is
followed by `:`; there is no handling of `=` anywhere in the parser, so the key is left
unquoted and `json.Unmarshal` fails. `repairGemma4SingleQuotedValues` is also anchored on
`:`, so both recovery paths miss the same case. The renderer emits `:` canonically, but
the model drifts to `=` — in our runs, most often when the *user prompt* itself contains
quoted `key='value'` assignments (68% parse success vs ~95% with a plain prompt, n=22/20).

Not length-related: 4.9KB `code` arguments parse fine; the failing argument is always the
2nd or later. `<|"|>` raw-string arguments themselves work.

Affected: v0.21.0 through v0.32.14 (`quoteGemma4BareKeys` is byte-identical across that
range). Related: #15241, #15315, #15539, PR #15255, PR #16075.

## Suggested fix

Accept `=` wherever `:` is accepted, in both `quoteGemma4BareKeys` and
`repairGemma4SingleQuotedValues`. We ported the parser algorithm to Python and replayed
our captured failing payloads: with `=` accepted, every observed failure parses and all
canonical forms are unchanged. (Simulation only — not yet validated against a patched
build.)

## Repro

1. Any tool with ≥2 string arguments (e.g. `code`, `save_as`).
2. A prompt that itself writes quoted assignments, e.g. "…and save it as
   save_as='report.docx'".
3. Repeat ~20×; a subset of responses come back with empty content and no tool_calls,
   with the parse warning in the server log.

items.title: Three bugs found running Gemma 4 / Qwen through a coding agent: repetition guard, truncated tool calls, gemma4 tool call dropped on a missing brace
items.body:
Hi all — three bugs found while running Gemma 4 A4B and Qwen A3B derivatives through a real coding agent (Cline) for several days. They are independent of each other and of the thinking-budget proposal I filed separately; each helps any tool-using model. I have a branch for each and I would rather agree the approach here first, because two of the three land in territory where work is already in flight.

Per CONTRIBUTING these are bug fixes rather than features, so an issue is not strictly required — I am opening one because the *direction* of two of them is arguable, and I would rather argue it before anyone reviews code.

---

## 1. A repetitive payload is treated as a runaway, and the abort is reported as success

A coding agent was asked to embed sound effects in a page. It ran

```
powershell -Command "[Convert]::ToBase64String([System.IO.File]::ReadAllBytes('sounds/coin.mp3'))"
```

fed the result back, and the next turn died with

> Did not receive done or success response in stream.

which names neither the model, the reason, nor the request. The server logged nothing: no error, no warning, and a `200`.

Two separate defects:

**The detector.** Generation is aborted after 31 identical tokens. Base64 of a binary file, a hex dump, a long run of indentation or a wide table of repeated values all reach that in normal, correct output. This is not a model looping; it is a model doing what it was asked.

**The reporting.** The abort is surfaced as success, so the stream simply ends with no `done` message. Every client raises the error above, and nothing on the server side records why.

**What I changed.** The run is measured in characters against a budget no real payload reaches, a repeating *unit* of up to 32 tokens is recognised rather than a single token, and a generation stopped this way terminates with `done_reason: "repeat"` so a client can tell what happened.

The reporting half is not arguable — a request that ends without `done` is a bug on any reading. The detector is the part worth discussing.

### How this relates to #15212

**#15212 "sample: add segment-level repetition loop detection"** (open, +407/−59, no comments since 2026-04-02) is adjacent but not the same thing, and I do not think either blocks the other:

| | #15212 | this |
| --- | --- | --- |
| layer | the sampler (`sample/samplers.go`, both runners, MLX) | the guard around generation (`llm/`) |
| goal | *escape* a loop by raising temperature when a segment repeats | stop *mis-firing* on legitimate repetitive output, and report properly when it does fire |
| failure addressed | the model genuinely loops | the model genuinely does not |
| default | off (`repeat_line_window=0`), four new options | no new options |

They compose: with #15212 enabled fewer real loops ever reach the guard, and this change stops the guard from killing base64. Neither fixes the other's problem — #15212 cannot make an aborted stream emit `done`, and no guard tuning breaks a model out of a loop. File overlap is nil (`llm/`, `openai/` here; `sample/`, `runner/`, `api/types.go` there).

Also related: **#16179** (MLX runner has no repetition loop detection or abort), **#16685** (qwen3.5 endless word salad), **#17459** (Gemma 4 repeated `<unused49>` when `think=false`).

---

## 2. A tool call cut off by the token limit is handed over as if it were complete

A response that ends on the token limit can stop in the middle of a tool call's arguments. The fields that already arrived parse cleanly, so the call reaches the caller looking finished, with a required argument simply absent. Captured from a Cline session against Gemma 4 with `num_predict` 32000:

```
tool:      editor
arguments: insert_line = 48
           new_text    = 62,288 characters   ← 76% base64
           (no path)
```

The caller reports a schema error naming a field the model was still writing. The user sees a validation failure; the actual event was truncation.

**What I changed.** Such a call is dropped rather than handed over — and only when the generation actually stopped at the limit, so a genuinely malformed call from a completed generation is unaffected.

### This is the opposite of what #15465 proposes, deliberately

**#15465 "fix: recover truncated tool call JSON when max_tokens cuts output"** (an *issue*, not a PR — no implementation, no comments since 2026-04-09) proposes the inverse: *"Add recovery for truncated tool call JSON so that at least the successfully parsed key-value pairs are returned rather than dropping the entire call."*

I think that is the wrong trade, and the reason is the case it does not mention. Recovery is only safe if truncation can be told from completeness, and the proposal has no mechanism for that: no schema check against the tool's declared required fields, and nothing at all about a truncated *value* as opposed to a missing *key*. Its own example is the dangerous one — `write_file{path, content}` cut mid-`content` yields

```
{"path": "index.html", "content": "<first 60% of the file>"}
```

which is well-formed, passes any schema check, and silently writes a truncated file. A missing key at least produces an error the caller can see; a truncated value produces a plausible call that does the wrong thing. Dropping is the conservative failure, and the model can be asked again.

Worth separating from a third approach already in flight: **#14835** and **#14915** (both open) convert *unparseable* qwen tool calls into **content** instead of erroring, which fixes #14570's 500. That is compatible with this change and I am not proposing to replace it — those handle output that does not parse, this handles output that parses but is incomplete. If maintainers prefer the truncated text to be surfaced as content rather than dropped outright, that composes with what I have and I am happy to do it that way.

Also related: **#12064** (tool call parsing errors, 27 comments), **#14570**.

---

## 3. A Gemma 4 tool call that is complete except for its final `}` is dropped silently

Gemma 4 sometimes emits its tool-call closing tag while omitting the last brace of the arguments object. The call is complete in every other respect — the model finished it — but parsing fails and the call is dropped, so the caller receives an empty response with no indication anything was attempted.

**What I changed.** The missing brace is repaired and the call parsed — but **only when the model emitted its closing tag**, which rules out truncation. That condition is the whole safety argument: closing an object that a token limit cut short would manufacture exactly the plausible-looking-but-wrong call that item 2 above exists to prevent. Once the model has closed the call itself, a missing brace is a formatting slip rather than an argument that never arrived.

### Relationship to #16075 — complementary, and it will conflict textually

**#16075 "parser: avoid premature Gemma4 tool call termination"** (open, +706/−38, same two files) fixes a different bug in the same parser: a literal `<tool_call|>` appearing *inside* an argument value used to end the call early, leaking the rest of the argument into content.

The two are mirror images of each other:

| | close tag | arguments object | fix |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **#16075** | missing or late | complete, balanced braces | flush the call anyway |
| **this** | present | missing its final `}` | repair the brace and parse |

Neither subsumes the other, and both are real. But #16075 is a large change to the same file — it adds an `error` return to `parseEvents` and `eat`, and introduces `parseGemma4ToolCallWithFallback` at exactly the call site this patch modifies — so a textual conflict is certain. **If #16075 lands first I will rebase onto it and fold this repair into its fallback path**, which is the natural home for it. It should not be reviewed as a competing approach.

### It does **not** fix #15315

Worth saying plainly, since the titles look similar. **#15315** ("gemma4:e4b still has tool parsing errors", 50 comments) reports a different failure — the Gemma string delimiter and quoting, e.g.

```
error="invalid character '`' looking for beginning of value"
error="invalid character '\'' looking for beginning of value"
```

One of its examples is a fully closed `}`-terminated call. That is a string-delimiter problem, not a missing brace, and #16075's `gemma4StringDelimiter` handling is much closer to it than anything here. I mention it only so nobody expects this change to close it.

Also related: **#15428** (closed — gemma4:26b returns a completely empty response), which is the same user-visible symptom from a different cause.

---

## What I am asking

Mainly: is the direction right on 1 and 2? Specifically —

- **the repeat detector**: is a character budget plus a repeating-unit check the shape you want, or would you rather the guard be removed entirely and the job left to sampler-level work like #15212? (The `done_reason` fix stands either way.)
- **truncated tool calls**: drop, or surface as content? I have argued against recovering partial arguments above, but if maintainers disagree I would rather know before the review than during it.

Item 3 is narrow and I think uncontroversial, modulo rebasing onto #16075.

Each change has tests, and each is independent — they can be taken in any order or separately.

Cheers,
ManniX

items.title: Tool-call output is silently discarded when the parse fails: empty content, no tool_calls, 40 completion tokens reported
items.body:
**This report has been corrected.** It originally claimed Ollama was discarding a *valid* tool call. That was wrong, and the details are in the comments. What follows is the corrected version. The remaining issue is that when a tool call fails to parse, the generated output is discarded with no way for a caller to see what happened.

### What happens

With `qwen2.5:7b-instruct` on Ollama 0.32.1, a request carrying a single tool comes back as an empty assistant message: no `content`, no `tool_calls`, `finish_reason` "stop". The response reports 40 completion tokens, so it says it generated 40 tokens and returns none of them. There is no error, no warning, and nothing in the response that distinguishes this from a model that simply chose to say nothing.

### What the model actually generated

Not visible from the API. I built v0.32.1 with #17284 applied, which returns the buffered output as content when no tool call is parsed, and re-ran the same request. The recovered output, `completion_tokens` 40, identical to the unpatched run:

```
<tool_call>
{"name": "Apply tags to a document", "arguments": {"document_id": "doc-17", "tags": ["alpha", "beta", "gamma"]}}
</tool_call>
```

The block is well-formed and the arguments are correct. The `name` is `"Apply tags to a document"`, which is the tool's **description**, not its name `tag_document`. No registered tool matches, so the parser rejects it.

**The parser is doing the right thing.** The model emitted the wrong field. The defect is that this is invisible: 40 tokens of near-correct, obviously-diagnosable output are dropped and the caller is given an empty string.

### Why the same weights work under llama.cpp

The original report leaned on a llama.cpp comparison: the same GGUF blob, served by `llama-server --jinja`, returns a correct tool call 12/12. I attributed that to Ollama's parser being at fault. That was the wrong conclusion.

llama.cpp constrains generation. It builds a GBNF grammar from the tool definitions and applies it lazily once the tool-call start token appears (`build_grammar` over `foreach_function(inputs.tools, ...)` in `common/chat.cpp`, with `grammar_lazy` set when tools are present and `tool_choice` is auto). The function name is constrained to the declared tools, so this failure cannot occur there. Ollama generates unconstrained and parses afterwards, so a model that puts the wrong string in `name` fails, and currently fails silently.

### Reproduction

```json
{
  "model": "qwen2.5:7b-instruct",
  "messages": [
    {
      "role": "user",
      "content": "Tag document doc-17 with exactly alpha, beta, and gamma in that order."
    }
  ],
  "tools": [
    {
      "type": "function",
      "function": {
        "name": "tag_document",
        "description": "Apply tags to a document.",
        "parameters": {
          "type": "object",
          "required": ["document_id", "tags"],
          "properties": {
            "document_id": { "type": "string" },
            "tags": { "type": "array", "items": { "type": "string" } }
          }
        }
      }
    }
  ],
  "tool_choice": "auto",
  "stream": false,
  "temperature": 0.0,
  "top_p": 1.0,
  "seed": 42,
  "max_tokens": 1024
}
```

Response:

```json
{"id":"chatcmpl-392","object":"chat.completion","created":1784508668,"model":"qwen2.5:7b-instruct","system_fingerprint":"fp_ollama","choices":[{"index":0,"message":{"role":"assistant","content":""},"finish_reason":"stop"}],"usage":{"prompt_tokens":229,"completion_tokens":40,"total_tokens":269}}
```

Deterministic across reps. `/api/chat` behaves the same, so this is not specific to the OpenAI-compatible layer. Streaming returns a single chunk with `content: ""` and `finish_reason` stop. A second tool description produced the same result.

### Environment

- Ollama 0.32.1, macOS 26.5.2, Apple Silicon (M4 Max).
- llama-server version 10050 (b15ca938a) for the comparison.
- Model `qwen2.5:7b-instruct`, blob `sha256-2bada8a7450677000f678be90653b85d364de7db25eb5ea54136ada5f3933730`, 4683073952 bytes, Q4_K_M. The same file for both servers.
- Patched build for the recovery: tag `v0.32.1` (`30c3903`) with #17284 applied cleanly, `go test -run TestContent ./tools/` passing.

### What I think is worth fixing

1. Do not discard generated output when no tool call parses. #17284 does exactly this and it turned an opaque failure into a one-request diagnosis.
2. The token accounting is still odd on its own terms: 40 completion tokens reported with zero bytes returned. Even with the output restored, an empty response with a nonzero `eval_count` seems worth surfacing rather than reporting as a clean completion.

Related: #12174 reports lost tool calls on qwen2.5-coder with an array-typed parameter and settled on the model being unreliable. Given what turned up here, some of those reports may be the same wrong-`name` failure, invisible for the same reason. #16932 shares the symptom but has a different cause in the ministral parser.

Happy to test a patch against this repro, or to run it across other models if that would help.

items.title: [Bug] Qwen3.8-27B: markdown image tag dropped from final response when using tools API parameter
items.body:
### What is the issue?

**What happened:**

When using qwen3.8:27b with a generate_image-style tool passed via the /api/chat `tools` parameter, the model consistently fails to include the tool's returned markdown image tag (`![...](...)`) in its final synthesized response — even when the tool result contains a valid markdown tag and the system prompt explicitly instructs the model to include it verbatim.

Instead, the model only describes the image in prose, omitting the actual markdown syntax entirely, so no image renders in any client (tested via Open-WebUI). This was 100% reproducible across 9-10 test runs, with both think:false and default thinking (on).

**Workaround confirmed:** Omitting the `tools` API parameter entirely and instead embedding the tool schema directly in the system prompt (Hermes-style JSON) resolves the issue — the model then correctly includes the markdown tag verbatim. This suggests the bug is tied to how Ollama constructs the prompt/context when the `tools` parameter is used, not a model-level flaw in Qwen3.8 itself.

This may be related to #14601, which documents other bugs specific to Qwen3 + the tools parameter, though that issue's most relevant sub-bug (tool call/result stripping) was later retracted as a client-side issue by the reporter — so this may be a distinct, still-unconfirmed root cause.

**What I expected:** The model's final response to include the literal markdown image tag returned by the tool, as instructed in the system prompt — matching behavior confirmed working when the same tool schema is embedded in the system prompt instead of passed via `tools`.

### Relevant log output

```shell
FAILING (tools parameter used — image markdown dropped from final response):

Request:
{
  "model": "qwen3.8:27b",
  "messages": [
    {"role": "user", "content": "What is the weather in <city>, <state>?"},
    {"role": "assistant", "content": "", "tool_calls": [{"id": "call_1", "function": {"name": "get_current_weather", "arguments": {"location": "<city>, <state>"}}}]},
    {"role": "tool", "content": "<city>, <state>: 78°F, partly cloudy, humidity 55%, wind 8 mph NW", "tool_call_id": "call_1"}
  ],
  "tools": [
    {"type": "function", "function": {"name": "get_current_weather", "description": "Get the current weather for a location", "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {"location": {"type": "string"}}, "required": ["location"]}}}
  ],
  "think": false,
  "stream": false
}

Note: the above is the weather-scenario synthesis test, which succeeded — included to show the tools-parameter path works fine for non-image tools. The actual failing case was the live generate_image tool in Open-WebUI, reproduced consistently over 9-10 runs. Representative failing response (image tool called successfully, tool result contained a valid markdown tag, but final response only described it in prose):

{"role":"assistant","content":"Here's your image — a red fox sitting in a snowy forest bathed in warm sunset light. 🦊\n\nWant me to tweak it (different pose, more/less snow, a different time of day, add a companion animal, etc.)?"}

Tool result that was available to the model but not carried forward:
![Generated image: A red fox sitting in a snowy forest at sunset](https://<domain>.com/images/8d580b0093...png)

System prompt in use (relevant excerpt):
"When generate_image returns a markdown image tag, include it verbatim plus a one-sentence confirmation - never output raw JSON/tool-call syntax as your visible response."

---

WORKING (tools parameter omitted, schema embedded in system prompt):

Request:
{
  "model": "qwen3.8:27b",
  "messages": [
    {"role": "system", "content": "You have access to the following tool:\n\n{\"type\": \"function\", \"function\": {\"name\": \"generate_image\", \"description\": \"Generate an image from a text description using Stable Diffusion.\", \"parameters\": {\"type\": \"object\", \"properties\": {\"prompt\": {\"type\": \"string\"}}, \"required\": [\"prompt\"]}}}\n\nWhen generate_image returns a markdown image tag, include it verbatim plus a one-sentence confirmation - never output raw JSON/tool-call syntax as your visible response."},
    {"role": "user", "content": "Generate an image of a fox sitting in a snowy forest at sunset"},
    {"role": "assistant", "content": "", "tool_calls": [{"id": "call_1", "function": {"name": "generate_image", "arguments": {"prompt": "A red fox sitting in a snowy forest at sunset"}}}]},
    {"role": "tool", "content": "![Generated image: A red fox sitting in a snowy forest at sunset](https://<domain>.com/images/test123.png)", "tool_call_id": "call_1"}
  ],
  "think": false,
  "stream": false
}

Response:
{"model":"qwen3.8:27b","created_at":"2026-08-15T02:56:26.4678218Z","message":{"role":"assistant","content":"Here's your fox sitting in a snowy forest at sunset — a serene winter scene bathed in warm, golden light.\n\n![Generated image: A red fox sitting in a snowy forest at sunset](https://<domain>.com/images/test123.png)"},"done":true,"done_reason":"stop","total_duration":9199905200,"load_duration":8093737400,"prompt_eval_count":217,"prompt_eval_duration":349819000,"eval_count":57,"eval_duration":753497000}

Note the markdown image tag is correctly preserved verbatim in the response when the tools parameter is omitted and the schema is embedded directly in the system prompt instead — same model, same instruction, only difference is the tools-parameter path.

---

Ollama version: 0.32.13
Model: qwen3.8:27b (Q4_K_M)
OS: Windows
Client: Open-WebUI (live testing) + raw curl against /api/chat (isolated reproduction)
```

### OS

Windows

Nvidia

items.title: model/parsers: cohere parser never sees its end-of-turn boundary on llama-server
items.body:
### What happens

The cohere parser depends on `<|END_OF_TURN_TOKEN|>` as a block boundary, but does not list it in `PreservedTokens()`. llama-server only renders special tokens that appear in `preserved_tokens`, so the parser never receives it.

When a turn closes its text block with the end-of-turn marker instead of `<|END_TEXT|>` and then opens an action block, the parser stays in the content-collecting state and the entire tool call is streamed to the user as literal text. No tool call is emitted.

### Where

`model/parsers/cohere.go:57` omits `cohereEndOfTurn` from `PreservedTokens()`, while the parser relies on that constant at four sites:

- `cohere.go:174` closes a content block on it. The comment there is explicit about the intent: `// END_OF_TURN also closes content for models that skip END_TEXT.`
- `cohere.go:151` consumes it between blocks in `cohereAwaitingBlock`
- `cohere.go:182` keeps back a partial suffix of it
- `cohere.go:223` lists it in `maybePartialTag`

The stripping is by design on the llama-server side. From `llm/llama_server.go:1421`:

```go
// llama-server only preserves strings that tokenize to one special token.
```

So the fallback branch at `cohere.go:174` is unreachable whenever the model runs on llama-server.

### Reproduction

Running the parser directly on the same turn, once with the token present and once with it stripped the way llama-server would strip it:

```go
stream := `t<|END_THINKING|><|START_TEXT|>hi<|END_OF_TURN_TOKEN|>` +
    `<|START_ACTION|>[{"tool_call_id":"1","tool_name":"get_weather","parameters":{"city":"SF"}}]<|END_ACTION|><|END_OF_TURN_TOKEN|>`
```

| Input | content | tool calls |
| --- | --- | --- |
| token preserved | `"hi"` | 1 (`get_weather`) |
| token stripped (llama-server today) | `"hi<\|START_ACTION\|>[{\"tool_call_id\":\"1\",...}]<\|END_ACTION\|>"` | **0** |

Identical result whether the stream arrives as one chunk or character by character.

### Why it matters

The two failure properties are the bad ones: it is silent, and it is backend-dependent.

`llm/server.go:214` documents `PreservedTokens` as `ignored by non-llama-server runners`, so the MLX runner passes the token through and parses the turn correctly. The same model and the same prompt produce a working tool call on MLX and a tool call rendered as raw text on llama-server. There is no error and nothing in the logs.

### Why it was not caught

Every existing test in `model/parsers/cohere_test.go` feeds `<|END_OF_TURN_TOKEN|>` to the parser literally, which encodes the assumption that the token reaches the parser. That assumption holds in the unit tests and fails in production on llama-server.

More generally, `PreservedTokens()` is a contract documented on the `Parser` interface and enforced only by each implementation remembering to list its own tokens. I audited all 26 parsers by diffing the special-token literals each one matches on against what it returns from `PreservedTokens()`. Cohere is the only violation, so this is a one-off rather than a systemic gap, but nothing would catch the next one.

### Proposed fix

Add `cohereEndOfTurn` to `PreservedTokens()`, and add two tests: one that parses a text-then-action turn separated by the end-of-turn marker, and one that asserts the token stays in `PreservedTokens()` so a future edit cannot drop it again.

One line of production code, 33 lines of test. `go test ./model/... ./server/... ./llm/... ./api/...` passes; `gofmt` and `go vet` are clean. The guard test fails without the fix.

I have the patch ready and am happy to open a PR.

### Documentation

No user-facing documentation changes. The behavior being fixed is the one the code already documents at `cohere.go:173`.

### What I did not verify

I did not run llama-server against real Cohere weights. The stripping behavior is taken from ollama's own comment at `llm/llama_server.go:1421` and the field documentation at `llm/server.go:214`, combined with the parser's coded expectation. The divergence table above comes from executing the parser itself, not the full stack.

items.title: fix: recover truncated tool call JSON when max_tokens cuts output
items.body:
## Problem

When a model generates a large tool call (e.g., `write_file` with HTML content), the JSON arguments can be truncated if the output hits the token limit. The tool call is silently dropped instead of returning partial arguments.

This causes missing tool calls when:
- `write_file` produces large HTML/code content
- Qwen3/Gemma4 models hit their output token limit mid-JSON

## Proposed Fix

Add recovery for truncated tool call JSON so that at least the successfully parsed key-value pairs are returned rather than dropping the entire call.

## Reproduction

```bash
curl http://localhost:11434/api/chat -d '{
  "model": "qwen3:8b",
  "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Write a complete HTML dashboard page"}],
  "tools": [{"type": "function", "function": {"name": "write_file", "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {"path": {"type": "string"}, "content": {"type": "string"}}}}}],
  "options": {"num_predict": 2048}
}'
```

Tool call JSON gets truncated, no tool_calls in response.

Note: PRs #14835/#14915 fix this for model-specific parsers (Qwen3, etc.). This fix targets the generic `tools/tools.go` parser used when no model-specific parser is available.

items.title: deepseek-v4-flash:cloud: model-leaked literal </think> in assistant history locks agentic clients into a self-sustaining tool-call loop (193 identical calls, ~31M tokens)
items.body:
# What is the issue?

`deepseek-v4-flash:cloud`, driven by Claude Code through the Anthropic-compat endpoint (`ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:11434`, requests visible in the server log as `POST /v1/messages?beta=true`), degenerated into a **self-sustaining loop: 193 consecutive responses, each containing near-identical garbage text plus the exact same tool call**, until a human interrupted. Each iteration was a full ~162k-token prompt against Ollama Cloud — roughly **31M input tokens** consumed by the loop.

I believe the lock-in mechanism is the one already confirmed in #17248: a literal `</think>` that reaches message content is reinterpreted as a template delimiter instead of being preserved as text. Here the tag entered through the other door — the **model's own output**. Once one degenerate response containing a literal `</think>` landed in the assistant history, the agentic client faithfully replayed it on every subsequent request, the template presumably split the prompt at that literal tag the same way each time, and the model reproduced the same broken continuation indefinitely. The client executes whatever tool call comes back, so the loop feeds itself and nothing model-side ever breaks it.

## Timeline (from the client transcript)

1. Normal operation for ~380 assistant messages. Reasoning arrived correctly as separate `thinking` blocks throughout (the compat layer's think parsing was working).
2. At ~162k input tokens, output degraded gradually: a `text` block of just `rath`, then `inkrath` — ordinary long-context repetition wobble.
3. Then the loop locked in. Every response became: one short garbage `text` block + the identical Bash `tool_use` (`cd <repo> && grep -n "rebuild" crates/policy/src/defs/rebuild.rs | head -8`). 193 iterations.
4. Only a human interrupt ended it. After the interrupt injected a new user message, the **same session recovered completely** — normal thinking blocks and correct behavior up to 259k input tokens.

## The leaked tags

The garbage `text` blocks are fragments of a short repeating token cycle, and many contain a **raw, unbalanced `</think>`** — a literal tag delivered in the `text` channel of `/v1/messages` responses. Distinct variants and counts across the 193 loop responses:

| count | literal `text` block content |
|---|---|
| 88 | `ink responserath` |
| 44 | `ink</think>rath` |
| 31 | `rath` |
| 31 | `ink responserathink response` |
| 8 | `rathink response` |
| 5 | `rathink</think>rath` |
| 5 | `ink</think>` |
| 3 | `ink response` |
| 2 | `rathink responserath` |

A literal `</think>` should never be able to reach the `text` channel unescaped — and per #17248, once it is replayed back in as content, prompt processing splits on it. The combination turns a one-off sampling wobble into an unbreakable loop for any agentic client.

## Secondary symptom: usage reporting froze

Every response during the loop reported exactly `"input_tokens": 162214, "output_tokens": 0` — frozen across all 193 calls, despite each response containing text and a tool call, and despite the history growing each iteration. Before and after the loop, usage numbers varied normally. This looks like the usage plumbing on the compat path also breaks while the stream is in this state (possibly related to #17130).

## Why this deserves attention beyond #17248

#17248 demonstrates the corruption with a literal `</think>` deliberately placed in user content. This report shows the tag can be **injected by the model itself** under long-context degeneration, after which the template-splitting behavior makes the failure self-sustaining and expensive: agentic clients (Claude Code, and presumably any tool-loop client) will replay the corrupted history forever. Cost here was ~31M input tokens for a single stuck session; nothing server-side or client-side ever terminates it.

Suggested fixes, in order of leverage:
1. Escape or strip think-delimiter literals when rendering **message content** into the prompt (the #17248 fix) — this breaks the feedback loop even if the model wobbles.
2. Never emit a literal `</think>` in the `text` channel of the compat APIs — if tag parsing desyncs mid-stream, drop or escape the delimiter rather than passing it through.

Related: #17248 (literal `</think>` corrupted in message content, same model among the repros), #16375 (raw DSML markup leaking into output on `deepseek-v4-flash:cloud` — same special-token handling class).

## Relevant log output

```shell
[GIN] 2026/08/07 - 23:29:59 | 200 | 12.157298167s | 127.0.0.1 | POST "/v1/messages?beta=true"
```

(server log shows only the routine 200s; all evidence above is from the client-side transcript of the `/v1/messages` responses)

### OS

macOS (darwin-arm64)

### GPU

Apple

### CPU

Apple

### Ollama version

server 0.32.6 (client 0.32.4)

items.title: Cloud models: tool_call.function.arguments truncated or 502 Bad Gateway when outputting large content
items.body:
## Bug Description

When using Ollama Cloud models via the Cloud API (`https://ollama.com/v1`) or local proxy (`http://localhost:11434/v1`) with tool definitions, `tool_call.function.arguments` is either truncated or results in a `502 Bad Gateway` error when the model attempts to output large content through a tool call. Both endpoints exhibit identical behavior — the issue is server-side on Ollama's cloud infrastructure, not the client proxy.

This makes agent workflows that rely on tool calls to write files unreliable or completely broken.

## Environment

- **Ollama version**: 0.23.0
- **Model**: `kimi-k2.6:cloud` (also affects `glm-5.1:cloud`, `qwen3.5:397b`)
- **Endpoints tested**: Both `https://ollama.com/v1/chat/completions` and `http://localhost:11434/v1/chat/completions` — same results
- **Plan**: Pro
- **Context length**: 262,144 (cloud default, confirmed via `ollama show`)

## Reproduction

Send a request to either endpoint with tool definitions. The model generates a `write_file` tool call. As the requested output size increases, the behavior degrades:

### Test 1: Small file (~40 lines) — Works ✅

```json
POST https://ollama.com/v1/chat/completions
(or equivalently http://localhost:11434/v1/chat/completions)

{
  "model": "kimi-k2.6:cloud",
  "messages": [
    {"role": "system", "content": "You are a helpful coding assistant. Always use the write_file tool to write files with ALL content."},
    {"role": "user", "content": "Write a file called test.py with a simple Flask app, about 40 lines."}
  ],
  "stream": false,
  "tools": [{"type": "function", "function": {"name": "write_file", "description": "Write content to a file", "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {"path": {"type": "string"}, "content": {"type": "string"}}, "required": ["path", "content"]}}}]
}
```

**Result**: `tool_call.function.arguments` length ~950-1100 chars. Content is complete and valid JSON.

### Test 2: Medium file (~60 lines) — Intermittent 502 ⚠️

Same request but asking for ~60 lines. After 3 consecutive attempts:

| Attempt | Result |
|---------|--------|
| 1 | ✅ OK: args_len=2058, 68 lines |
| 2 | ✅ OK: args_len=2054, 61 lines |
| 3 | ❌ HTTP 502 Bad Gateway |

### Test 3: Large file (100+ lines) — Consistent 502 ❌

Requesting 100+ lines of code reliably results in `502 Bad Gateway`.

### Test 4: Very large file (200+ lines) — Immediate EOF ❌

```json
{"error":"Post \"https://ollama.com:443/v1/chat/completions?ts=1778353283\": unexpected EOF"}
```

Both endpoints (`ollama.com/v1` and `localhost:11434/v1`) produce identical failures, confirming the issue is on Ollama's cloud server side.

## Key Observations

1. **No API parameter controls tool_call size**: The OpenAI compatibility endpoint (`/v1/chat/completions`) has no parameter to control `tool_call.function.arguments` maximum length. `max_tokens` only controls total generation tokens, not individual tool call argument size.

2. **Cloud models have no Modelfile**: `ollama show kimi-k2.6:cloud --modelfile` returns empty. Users cannot set `num_ctx` or other parameters via Modelfile for cloud models.

3. **The truncation/502 is server-side**: Both direct Cloud API (`https://ollama.com/v1`) and local proxy (`http://localhost:11434/v1`) produce identical failures. The local proxy merely forwards to `ollama.com:443`. Per docs, _Cloud models are set to their maximum context length by default_ — context length is not the bottleneck.

4. **Non-tool-call output works fine**: Regular text responses (without tool_calls) with large content do not trigger 502 errors, suggesting the issue is specific to how the cloud handles structured `tool_call.function.arguments` in buffering/streaming.

5. **Both endpoints affected identically**: Whether calling `https://ollama.com/v1/chat/completions` directly or proxying through `http://localhost:11434/v1/chat/completions`, the same truncation/502 pattern occurs — eliminating any local Ollama proxy as the cause.

## Expected Behavior

`tool_call.function.arguments` should contain complete, valid JSON regardless of content length, up to the model's context window limit (256K for kimi-k2.6:cloud). If there is a server-side limit, it should be documented and the API should return a clear error instead of a 502 or silent truncation.

## Impact

This makes Ollama Cloud models effectively unusable for agent workflows that write files via tool calls (e.g., coding assistants, automated code generation). Any file over ~40 lines cannot be reliably written in a single tool call.

## Suggested Fixes

1. **Increase or remove the tool_call arguments buffer limit** on the Ollama Cloud proxy.
2. **If a limit must exist**, document it clearly and return a proper 4xx error instead of 502 when exceeded.
3. **Consider chunked/streaming delivery** of large tool_call arguments to avoid single-buffer limits.

items.title: qwen3.6 occasionally violates its own tool-call template; qwen3.5 parser returns 500 instead of tolerating the drift
items.body:
### What is the issue?

`qwen3.6:27b` (and the other qwen3.6 tags) registers `PARSER qwen3.5` / `RENDERER qwen3.5`. With `tools[]` populated on a chat completion, the qwen3.5 parser intermittently fails to unmarshal qwen3.6's tool-call output and Ollama returns 500. The bug is intermittent: simple curl tests usually succeed, but cumulatively painful for any agent that issues many tool-using calls in a session.

#### Root cause appears to be model drift, not a wrong parser

Qwen's official `tokenizer_config.json` for `Qwen/Qwen3.6-27B` specifies the same `<tool_call><function=…><parameter=…>…</parameter></function></tool_call>` format Ollama's qwen3.5 renderer expects, with this `<IMPORTANT>` reminder in the template:

> "Function calls MUST follow the specified format: an inner `<function=...></function>` block must be nested within `<tool_call></tool_call>` XML tags"

So the renderer/parser pair is structurally correct against Qwen's stated spec. The bug is that **qwen3.6 doesn't reliably follow its own template** — it intermittently drifts to what looks like an older `<function_invocation>…</function_invocation>` wrapper. Evidence below.

#### Evidence — model emits malformed XML

Bypassing the parser (no `tools[]` field), asking qwen3.6:27b to emit a tool call as XML:

```bash
curl http://localhost:11434/api/chat -d '{
  "model": "qwen3.6:27b",
  "stream": false,
  "think": false,
  "messages": [
    {"role":"system","content":"You are a helpful assistant. When you need to call a function, emit it in XML form with <function=name> wrapping <parameter=key>value</parameter> elements. Always make the call."},
    {"role":"user","content":"What is the weather in Paris? Use the function get_weather(location: string)."}
  ]
}'
```

`message.content` returned (107 chars verbatim):

```
<function=get_weather>
<parameter=location>Paris</parameter>
</function>
</function>
</function_invocation>
```

Two issues:

1. **Spurious extra `</function>`** close tag.
2. **`</function_invocation>` close tag** with no matching open — looks like a leak from an older training format.

When the same model is invoked with `tools[]` populated, the qwen3.5 renderer wraps the conversation with `<tool_call>` instructions and qwen3.6 mostly complies. But when the drift occurs inside a `<tool_call>` block, `parseToolCall` → `xml.Unmarshal` rejects the input because the first child element is `<parameter>` (or stray garbage) rather than `<function>`.

#### Reproducing the 500 directly

A small single-shot curl with a `tools[]` field does **not** reliably fail (tested 20× — 20/20 200 OK). Failures cluster on longer multi-iteration turns with substantial conversation history. Bypassing the parser as shown above is the cleanest reproduction of the underlying model behavior; the parser error is then a consequence of that behavior reaching the unmarshal path.

`ollama show qwen3.6:27b` returns:

```
RENDERER qwen3.5
PARSER   qwen3.5
```

#### Suggested fix (Ollama side — defense-in-depth)

Tighten the existing qwen3.5 parser (`model/parsers/qwen3coder.go`) to tolerate this specific drift: inside a `<tool_call>` block, anchor on the first `<function=…>` opening tag and skip any stray closing tags / unmatched wrappers (`</function>`, `</function_invocation>`) before handing to `xml.Unmarshal`. Localized change, avoids any model-manifest churn, and the failure mode is well-characterized by the captured output above.

A complementary upstream fix at the Qwen team would address the root cause, but as a downstream consumer the parser-tolerance change unblocks users today.

Happy to PR the parser-tolerance change if there's interest — let me know.

#### Related code paths (main)

- `model/parsers/qwen3coder.go:64` — `parseToolCall` returning the unmarshal error
- `model/parsers/qwen35.go:96` — wrapper logging the same error
- `model/renderers/qwen35.go:1-36` — the prompt format the model is told to use

### Relevant log output

```shell
time=2026-05-31T21:24:28.906Z level=WARN source=qwen3coder.go:64 msg="qwen tool call parsing failed" error="expected element type <function> but have <parameter>"
time=2026-05-31T21:24:28.906Z level=WARN source=qwen35.go:96 msg="qwen3.5 tool call parsing failed" error="expected element type <function> but have <parameter>"
[GIN] 2026/05/31 - 21:24:28 | 500 |   4.07683667s | POST     "/api/chat"
```

### OS

Linux

### GPU

Nvidia

### CPU

Intel

### Ollama version

0.24.0

items.title: ollama pull hf.co/... doesn't apply the built-in RENDERER/PARSER for recognized architectures, causing unreliable tool-calling

labels.name: networking
labels.description: Issues relating to ollama pull and push

items.body:
## Summary

When pulling a GGUF directly from Hugging Face (`ollama pull hf.co/<repo>:<tag>`), Ollama correctly detects the model's architecture (e.g. `qwen3moe`) and lists `tools` as a capability — but it does **not** assign the built-in, natively-coded `RENDERER`/`PARSER` pair that the same architecture gets when pulled from Ollama's own curated library (e.g. `qwen3-coder`). Instead it falls back to an auto-generated generic Go template that relies on the model reliably free-forming the exact `<tool_call>` XML tag in its raw text output.

In practice, this makes tool-calling **unreliable to completely broken** for `hf.co`-pulled models, even though Ollama already has the correct native renderer/parser for that exact architecture built in and uses it automatically for its own library models.

## Environment

- Ollama version: 0.31.2 (AMD "AI Bundle" build, Windows)
- OS: Windows 11 Pro
- GPU: AMD Radeon RX 7800 XT, 16GB VRAM, ROCm backend (gfx1101)
- Affected model: `hf.co/unsloth/Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct-GGUF` — tested at both `UD-Q2_K_XL` and `UD-Q3_K_XL` tags

## Steps to reproduce

1. `ollama pull hf.co/unsloth/Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct-GGUF:UD-Q2_K_XL`
2. Send a request to `/api/chat` (or the OpenAI-compatible `/v1/chat/completions`) with a `tools` array defined, e.g.:
   ```json
   {
     "model": "hf.co/unsloth/Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct-GGUF:UD-Q2_K_XL",
     "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "List the files in the current directory."}],
     "tools": [{"type": "function", "function": {"name": "Bash", "description": "Run a bash command", "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {"command": {"type": "string"}}, "required": ["command"]}}}],
     "stream": false,
     "options": {"temperature": 0}
   }
   ```
3. Observe the response.

## Actual behavior

The model's tool-call attempt leaks into the `content` field as raw, malformed text instead of a structured `tool_calls` field. Reproducible at `temperature: 0` (not a sampling-randomness issue):

```json
{"message":{"role":"assistant","content":"{\"name\": \"Bash\", \"arguments\": {\"command\": \"ls -l\"}}\n</tool_call>"}}
```

Note the missing opening `<tool_call>` tag (only the stray closing tag survives). Tested at `UD-Q3_K_XL` too — same failure, slightly different malformation (no tags at all that time):

```json
{"message":{"role":"assistant","content":"{\"name\": \"Bash\", \"arguments\": {\"command\": \"ls -l\"}}"}}
```

Since the failure is essentially identical across two different quantization levels of the same GGUF conversion, this doesn't look like quantization-noise — it looks like the generic auto-generated template/parsing path is simply less robust than the native one.

## Expected behavior

A structured `tool_calls` field, e.g. what the *official* `qwen3-coder:30b` library model correctly returns for the identical request:

```json
{"message":{"role":"assistant","content":"","tool_calls":[{"id":"call_...","function":{"name":"Bash","arguments":{"command":"ls -l"}}}]}}
```

## Root cause (as far as I could tell)

Comparing `ollama show <model> --modelfile` between the broken and working model:

- **Official `qwen3-coder:30b`** (works correctly):
  ```
  TEMPLATE {{ .Prompt }}
  RENDERER qwen3-coder
  PARSER qwen3-coder
  ```
- **`hf.co/unsloth/Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct-GGUF:UD-Q2_K_XL`** (broken): gets a long auto-generated Go `TEMPLATE` (derived from the GGUF's embedded chat template) with **no `RENDERER`/`PARSER` directive at all**.

`ollama show` on the `hf.co` pull correctly reports:
```
architecture   qwen3moe
...
Capabilities
  completion
  tools
```

So Ollama *does* know this is a `qwen3moe`/tool-capable model — it just doesn't connect that recognition to the already-existing native `qwen3-coder` renderer/parser pair unless the model was pulled from Ollama's own library.

## Workaround (confirmed working)

Creating a custom Modelfile pointing at the *same* downloaded blob, but explicitly adding the renderer/parser directives, fixes it completely with no downsides found:

```
FROM <path-to-existing-blob>
TEMPLATE {{ .Prompt }}
RENDERER qwen3-coder
PARSER qwen3-coder
PARAMETER stop <|im_start|>
PARAMETER stop <|im_end|>
PARAMETER temperature 0.7
PARAMETER min_p 0
PARAMETER repeat_penalty 1.05
PARAMETER top_k 20
PARAMETER top_p 0.8
```

```
ollama create qwen3-coder-ud-q2-fixed -f Modelfile
```

Verified after the fix:
- Correct structured `tool_calls` on both the native `/api/chat` and OpenAI-compatible `/v1/chat/completions` endpoints.
- Decode speed unaffected (~57 tok/s before and after, measured over several prompts).
- Plain-text queries (tools available but not needed) are still answered as plain text — the fix doesn't force tool-call mode indiscriminately.

## Suggested fix

When `ollama pull hf.co/...` detects an architecture (and ideally a matching tokenizer/template signature) that corresponds to a model family Ollama already ships a native `RENDERER`/`PARSER` for (like `qwen3-coder`), apply that same renderer/parser automatically instead of (or as a preferred fallback over) the generic auto-generated template — the same way it's already applied for the equivalent official library model.

---
*Note: [Unsloth's own docs](https://unsloth.ai/docs/models/tutorials/qwen3-coder-how-to-run-locally) state tool-calling fixes for Ollama were "already included in the 30B model uploads" — that doesn't appear to hold for this specific pull path, which suggests the gap is on the Ollama side (missing renderer/parser assignment) rather than in the GGUF/template itself.*

items.title: /v1/chat/completions: content: "" on assistant messages with tool_calls causes model template rendering issues
items.body:
## Description

When the `/v1/chat/completions` endpoint receives assistant messages in the conversation history with `content: ""` (empty string) alongside `tool_calls`, models like `qwen3-coder` switch from structured tool calling to text-based markup mode on subsequent turns.

The `/v1` OpenAI-compatible layer should normalize `content: ""` to `content: null` (or treat them equivalently) before feeding messages to the model template, since the OpenAI API spec treats both as "no text content."

## Reproduction

```bash
# Turn 3 with content: "" in prior assistant messages → BROKEN
# Model switches to <function=write_file> text markup instead of structured tool_calls
curl -s http://localhost:11434/v1/chat/completions -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{
  "model": "qwen3-coder:latest",
  "stream": false,
  "messages": [
    {"role": "system", "content": "You are a helpful coding assistant. Use the provided tools to complete tasks."},
    {"role": "user", "content": "Can you help me build a todo list app?"},
    {"role": "assistant", "content": "", "tool_calls": [{"id": "call_1", "type": "function", "function": {"name": "list_files", "arguments": "{\"directory\":\".\"}"}  }]},
    {"role": "tool", "tool_call_id": "call_1", "content": "src/\npackage.json\nREADME.md"},
    {"role": "assistant", "content": "", "tool_calls": [{"id": "call_2", "type": "function", "function": {"name": "read_file", "arguments": "{\"path\":\"package.json\"}"}}]},
    {"role": "tool", "tool_call_id": "call_2", "content": "{\"name\": \"my-app\", \"dependencies\": {\"react\": \"^18\"}}"},
    {"role": "user", "content": "Great, now create the App.js with a basic todo list component"}
  ],
  "tools": [
    {"type": "function", "function": {"name": "list_files", "description": "List files in a directory", "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {"directory": {"type": "string"}}, "required": ["directory"]}}},
    {"type": "function", "function": {"name": "read_file", "description": "Read contents of a file", "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {"path": {"type": "string"}}, "required": ["path"]}}},
    {"type": "function", "function": {"name": "write_file", "description": "Write content to a file", "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {"path": {"type": "string"}, "content": {"type": "string"}}, "required": ["path", "content"]}}}
  ]
}'
# Result: finish_reason: "stop", content contains <function=write_file>{...}</function> text markup
# Expected: finish_reason: "tool_calls", structured tool_calls array
```

```bash
# Same conversation with non-empty content in history → WORKS
curl -s http://localhost:11434/v1/chat/completions -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{
  "model": "qwen3-coder:latest",
  "stream": false,
  "messages": [
    {"role": "system", "content": "You are a helpful coding assistant. Use the provided tools to complete tasks."},
    {"role": "user", "content": "Can you help me build a todo list app?"},
    {"role": "assistant", "content": "Sure! Let me check what files exist first.", "tool_calls": [{"id": "call_1", "type": "function", "function": {"name": "list_files", "arguments": "{\"directory\":\".\"}"}  }]},
    {"role": "tool", "tool_call_id": "call_1", "content": "src/\npackage.json\nREADME.md"},
    {"role": "assistant", "content": "I see you have a React project. Let me read the package.json.", "tool_calls": [{"id": "call_2", "type": "function", "function": {"name": "read_file", "arguments": "{\"path\":\"package.json\"}"}}]},
    {"role": "tool", "tool_call_id": "call_2", "content": "{\"name\": \"my-app\", \"dependencies\": {\"react\": \"^18\"}}"},
    {"role": "user", "content": "Great, now create the App.js with a basic todo list component"}
  ],
  "tools": [...]
}'
# Result: finish_reason: "tool_calls", clean structured tool_calls array ✓
```

The only difference is `content: ""` vs `content: "Sure! Let me check..."` on the assistant messages.

## Root cause

The `/v1` compatibility layer passes `content: ""` through to the model template renderer. For qwen3-coder (which uses `RENDERER qwen3-coder` / `PARSER qwen3-coder`), an empty string is rendered differently from null/absent content, causing the model to lose its tool-calling mode on subsequent turns.

## Expected behavior

The `/v1` endpoint should normalize `content: ""` to `null` on assistant messages that have `tool_calls`, since per the OpenAI spec both represent "no text content." This would make template rendering consistent regardless of whether the client sends `""` or `null`.

This is particularly impactful because the Vercel AI SDK (`@ai-sdk/openai`) sends `content: ""` for tool-call-only assistant messages (filed as https://github.com/vercel/ai/issues/12389), making this a common real-world pattern.

## Environment

- Ollama 0.9.x
- Model: qwen3-coder:latest
- Also likely affects other models with complex tool-call templates

items.title: Quantized KV cache (q8_0/q4_0) causes model to stop generating mid-turn instead of emitting a tool call, on qwen3.5/qwen3.6 (qwen35/qwen35moe) architecture under ROCm — severity tracks quant precision
items.body:
### What is the issue?

## Environment
- Ollama version: 0.31.1
- Backend: ROCm (`library=ROCm`)
- GPU: AMD Radeon RX 7900 XTX
- ROCm version: 7.2.1 (core), driver 6.19.4
- OS: Ubuntu 26.04 LTS, kernel 6.8.0-124-generic
- `OLLAMA_FLASH_ATTENTION=1` (explicitly set — required for KV cache quantization)
- Client: pi-coding-agent, via the `pi-ollama` provider plugin (v0.1.5), using the native `/api/chat` streaming endpoint (not the OpenAI-compat shim), `think: true` on every request

## Models tested
| Model | `general.architecture` | Params | Quant | Template/parser path |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `qwen3.6` (from a local qwen3.6-a3b-IQ4_XS GGUF) | `qwen35moe` | 34.7B (MoE) | IQ4_XS | Custom hand-written Go `TEMPLATE` in Modelfile |
| `qwen3.6:27b` | `qwen35` | 27.8B (dense) | Q4_K_M | Ollama's built-in renderer/parser (`renderer=qwen3.5 parser=qwen3.5`, `chat_template=[tools thinking completion vision]`) |

Note: neither `qwen35` nor `qwen35moe` appears in Ollama's `FlashAttention()` allowlist in `fs/ggml/ggml.go` (`gemma3`, `gptoss`/`gpt-oss`, `mistral3`, `qwen3`, `qwen3moe`, `qwen3vl`, `qwen3vlmoe`). Flash attention was force-enabled via `OLLAMA_FLASH_ATTENTION=1`, which does work per prior maintainer comments, but this means the architecture+FA+KV-quant combination is running outside Ollama's normal validated/default-enabled set.

## Symptom
In long agentic tool-calling sessions (both models, both template/parser paths), the model periodically stops generating with `done_reason: "stop"` and no tool call, right after writing a stated-intent sentence ending in a colon — e.g.:

> "Let me update the test file and do a full retest:"
> "Let me rewrite the entire file cleanly to avoid further issues:"
> "Still wrong. Let me verify the current state of `/home/z/md5.rb` to make sure my edits were applied:"

Instead of continuing into `<tool_call>...</tool_call>` (or the built-in parser's tool-call format), generation just ends. The client then has no tool call and no further text — from the user's perspective, the assistant "goes silent" and requires a manual "continue" to proceed.

Confirmed via `OLLAMA_NATIVE_DUMP_DIR`/`OLLAMA_NATIVE_DEBUG=1`  set on pi-coding in request/response captures that this is a genuine EOS from the model, not a client-side parsing bug: in every failing turn, `chunksReceived == outputTokens` exactly (nothing was dropped/swallowed by the streaming client).

## Ruled out
- Chat template `stop` sequences / EOS token misconfiguration (single correct `eos_token_id` in GGUF metadata; no `stop` Modelfile parameter set).
- Client-side `num_predict`/max-token caps (failures occur on short responses too; no `num_predict` override sent).
- The client's own OpenAI-compat tool-call-dropping issue (ollama#12557) — not applicable, client uses native `/api/chat` deliberately.
- Legacy `/think`/`/no_think` literal tags in content (confirmed inert in both template paths).
- `presence_penalty`/`temperature` Modelfile misconfiguration — fixed (`presence_penalty 0`, `temperature 0.6`, `repeat_penalty 1.1`) and confirmed live via server logs for every captured failing turn; failures persisted regardless.
- The system prompt encouraging narration before tool use — it explicitly says the opposite ("Be concise").
- Custom Modelfile `TEMPLATE` as the cause — same failure reproduces on Ollama's **built-in** `qwen3.5` renderer/parser (a completely different code path) on a different model (`qwen3.6:27b`, dense, Q4_K_M).

## Reproduction across KV cache types (same task class: implement + test an MD5 implementation from RFC 1321 in Ruby, agentic multi-turn session)

| `OLLAMA_KV_CACHE_TYPE` | Result |
|---|---|
| `q8_0` | Failed reliably. Across 7 real captured turns in one long session (156–168 messages), 3/7 hit the stall, first appearing at ~50–52k prompt tokens. The 4/7 successes were all turns where the model went straight into a tool call with no preceding prose. |
| `q4_0` | Failed almost immediately — same exact signature at only ~4.3k prompt tokens (`prompt_eval_count: 4275`, content ending "...Let me rewrite it cleanly:", `done_reason: "stop"`, `chunksReceived == outputTokens == 26`). |
| `f16` | No failures observed. Reproduced clean completion on both models: `qwen3.6:27b` completed a tool call at the same ~52k-token depth that had failed under `q8_0`; `qwen3.6:35b-a3b` completed an entire multi-turn session (full RFC 1321 MD5 implementation + test suite) using 64% of an 80k-token context budget with zero stalls. |

The failure rate tracks KV cache quantization severity, not context depth alone — `q4_0` (more aggressive) failed far earlier than `q8_0`, and `f16` (unquantized) showed no failures at all across comparable or longer sessions. This points at the quantized-KV attention path itself (not simply "more context = more error").

## Possibly related
- ollama/ollama#10945 — KV cache quantization breaking Gemma3 tool calling; root-caused to "features unsupported by the existing CUDA kernels, causing a fallback to CPU," fixed in Ollama 0.12.5. That fix was CUDA + Gemma3-specific and does not appear to cover this ROCm + qwen35/qwen35moe case (still reproduces on 0.31.1).
- ggml-org/llama.cpp#23873 — ROCm VRAM leak with quantized KV cache; reporter says resolved as of ~2026-06-12, uncertain whether via code fix or ROCm driver upgrade. This report is about VRAM growth, not generation-quality/tool-calling correctness, so may be a separate issue.
- ggml-org/llama.cpp Discussion #22411 — notes that on AMD HIP, symmetric quantized KV types route through a distinct fused Flash Attention kernel path versus unquantized/f16, which is a plausible mechanism for a ROCm-specific correctness gap like this one.

## Ask
Is this a known/tracked issue for the `qwen35`/`qwen35moe` architecture specifically? Given it's not in the FA default-allowlist, it's possible this exact combination (ROCm + forced FA + quantized KV + this newer Qwen3.5/3.6 architecture) simply hasn't been exercised much yet. Happy to provide the full request/response capture set (debug log + paired req/res dumps for both the q8_0 and q4_0 failures) if useful.

items.title: [Cloud] glm-5.3 can enter endless reasoning and eventually abort tasks in both OpenCode and ZCode, while official Z.AI works normally
items.body:
### What is the issue?

# [Cloud API] glm-5.3:cloud can enter endless reasoning and eventually abort tasks in both OpenCode and ZCode, while official Z.AI API works normally

## What is the issue?

I am experiencing a recurring issue with `glm-5.3:cloud` through the **Ollama Cloud API at ollama.com** with an **Ollama Pro subscription**.

I am **not running a local Ollama server/daemon**.

Both OpenCode and ZCode are configured to access Ollama Cloud directly through the Ollama API.

During agentic coding tasks, `glm-5.3:cloud` can enter an extremely long or apparently endless reasoning/thinking state. The model stops making meaningful progress, does not proceed to the next tool call or task step, and eventually the task/request terminates or is aborted.

The important point is that I can reproduce the same general behavior in **two different agent clients**:

- OpenCode + Ollama Cloud API + `glm-5.3:cloud`
- ZCode + Ollama Cloud API + `glm-5.3:cloud`

However, when I use my **official Z.AI subscription/API** with GLM-5.3 in the same clients, the issue does not occur:

- OpenCode + official Z.AI GLM-5.3 → works normally
- ZCode + official Z.AI GLM-5.3 → works normally

This makes me suspect that the problem may be somewhere in the **Ollama Cloud GLM-5.3 serving / reasoning / chat-template / API compatibility path**, rather than being caused exclusively by OpenCode, ZCode, or the GLM-5.3 model itself.

---

## Important clarification: no local Ollama installation is involved

My setup does **not** look like this:

```text
OpenCode / ZCode
       ↓
localhost:11434
       ↓
local Ollama
       ↓
Ollama Cloud
```

Instead, the clients access the **Ollama Cloud API directly**:

```text
OpenCode
   ↓
ollama.com Cloud API
   ↓
glm-5.3:cloud
```

and:

```text
ZCode
   ↓
ollama.com Cloud API
   ↓
glm-5.3:cloud
```

Therefore:

- there is no local Ollama daemon involved;
- there is no local Ollama model configuration involved;
- there is no localhost proxy or local Ollama OpenAI-compatible endpoint involved.

The common component in both failing setups is the **Ollama Cloud API + `glm-5.3:cloud`**.

---

## Important note about my OpenCode environment

My OpenCode installation has **Oh My OpenCode** installed.

I am mentioning this explicitly because Oh My OpenCode can affect prompts, agent behavior, tool orchestration, and execution flow, so it is a potential confounding factor when reproducing the issue specifically in OpenCode.

However, there are two important control observations.

### 1. ZCode also reproduces the issue

The same endless-thinking / eventual task-abort behavior occurs in **ZCode**, where Oh My OpenCode is not involved.

### 2. OpenCode + Oh My OpenCode works normally with official Z.AI

Using the same OpenCode environment, including Oh My OpenCode:

```text
OpenCode + Oh My OpenCode + Ollama Cloud glm-5.3:cloud
→ problem occurs

OpenCode + Oh My OpenCode + official Z.AI GLM-5.3
→ works normally
```

Therefore, Oh My OpenCode may influence the exact workload sent to the model, but it does not appear sufficient to explain the failure.

---

## Observed behavior

A typical failure looks approximately like this:

1. Start a coding-agent task using `glm-5.3:cloud` through the Ollama Cloud API.
2. The model initially behaves normally.
3. It performs reasoning and tool calls normally for some time.
4. During a later reasoning phase, thinking becomes extremely long or appears to stop making meaningful progress.
5. The model remains in the reasoning/thinking state instead of producing the next useful tool call or response.
6. Eventually the task/request terminates, aborts, times out, or otherwise fails to complete.

The behavior appears more likely during **long-running agentic coding tasks** than during simple single-turn questions.

Examples of workloads where I have observed this include tasks involving multiple iterations such as:

```text
inspect project
→ analyze files
→ plan changes
→ modify files
→ run tests
→ analyze failures
→ modify files again
→ continue agent workflow
```

The failure is not necessarily immediate. The agent may work normally for some time before entering the abnormal reasoning state.

---

## Expected behavior

`glm-5.3:cloud` should eventually complete its reasoning phase and do one of the following:

- produce the next tool call;
- continue the agent workflow;
- request additional information;
- or produce a final response.

It should not remain indefinitely in an apparently non-progressing reasoning state until the request or entire agent task is terminated.

---

## Cross-client / cross-provider comparison

| Client | Provider | Model | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| OpenCode + Oh My OpenCode | **Ollama Cloud API (ollama.com)** | `glm-5.3:cloud` | ❌ Can enter endless reasoning and eventually abort |
| ZCode | **Ollama Cloud API (ollama.com)** | `glm-5.3:cloud` | ❌ Can enter endless reasoning and eventually abort |
| OpenCode + Oh My OpenCode | **Official Z.AI API/subscription** | GLM-5.3 | ✅ Works normally |
| ZCode | **Official Z.AI API/subscription** | GLM-5.3 | ✅ Works normally |

This comparison is the main reason I suspect the Ollama Cloud implementation/path.

The same general clients and workloads are used, while changing the provider from Ollama Cloud to official Z.AI makes the problem disappear.

---

## Simplified comparison

```text
                   ┌─ Ollama Cloud glm-5.3:cloud
OpenCode + OMO ────┤
                   └─> endless reasoning / abort can occur

                   ┌─ official Z.AI GLM-5.3
OpenCode + OMO ────┤
                   └─> works normally
```

and independently:

```text
             ┌─ Ollama Cloud glm-5.3:cloud
ZCode ───────┤
             └─> endless reasoning / abort can occur

             ┌─ official Z.AI GLM-5.3
ZCode ───────┤
             └─> works normally
```

Because ZCode reproduces the problem independently of OpenCode / Oh My OpenCode, a purely OpenCode-specific explanation seems unlikely.

Because official Z.AI GLM-5.3 works normally in both clients, a problem inherent to all GLM-5.3 deployments also seems less likely.

---

## Steps to reproduce

The behavior is not completely deterministic, but it is much easier to observe during longer coding-agent tasks.

### OpenCode

1. Configure OpenCode to use the Ollama Cloud API directly.
2. Use an Ollama Pro account/API credential.
3. Select:

   `glm-5.3:cloud`

4. Run a long coding-agent task requiring multiple tool iterations.
5. Allow the agent to continue through multiple reasoning/tool turns.
6. Eventually the model may enter an unusually long reasoning state.
7. No useful next tool call is produced.
8. The task eventually terminates without completing normally.

My OpenCode environment also has:

**Oh My OpenCode installed.**

### ZCode

1. Configure ZCode to use the Ollama Cloud API directly.
2. Select:

   `glm-5.3:cloud`

3. Run a comparable long-running coding-agent task.
4. The same general endless-reasoning / eventual-abort behavior can occur.

### Control test

Configure the same clients to use my official Z.AI subscription/API with GLM-5.3.

In my experience:

```text
OpenCode + Z.AI GLM-5.3 → normal
ZCode + Z.AI GLM-5.3    → normal
```

The endless-reasoning behavior has not occurred there under comparable usage.

---

## Why I suspect the Ollama Cloud path

There are several reasons.

### 1. It reproduces in multiple independent clients

Both OpenCode and ZCode exhibit the problem when using Ollama Cloud.

This makes an OpenCode-specific bug unlikely to be the entire explanation.

### 2. No local Ollama component exists

Both clients connect directly to ollama.com.

Therefore the problem cannot be explained by:

- a local Ollama version;
- a local model template;
- localhost networking;
- a locally modified Modelfile;
- or local Ollama daemon configuration.

### 3. Official Z.AI GLM-5.3 works normally

Changing only the provider/backend is enough to make the issue disappear in my normal usage.

This suggests that there may be a behavioral difference between:

```text
official Z.AI GLM-5.3 API
```

and:

```text
Ollama Cloud glm-5.3:cloud
```

especially in long multi-turn tool-calling conversations.

---

## Possible areas to investigate

Could you please investigate whether the Ollama Cloud implementation of `glm-5.3:cloud` differs from the official Z.AI API in any of the following areas?

- reasoning/thinking history handling between turns;
- preservation of previous assistant reasoning;
- `clear_thinking` behavior;
- default reasoning effort;
- `reasoning_effort` translation;
- reasoning token streaming;
- reasoning → tool-call transitions;
- tool-result → next reasoning transitions;
- GLM chat-template construction;
- handling of assistant messages containing reasoning;
- maximum reasoning/output limits;
- stop conditions;
- finish reasons;
- server-side timeout/watchdog behavior;
- long multi-turn agent conversation handling;
- OpenAI-compatible / Anthropic-compatible API translation, if applicable.

I am particularly interested in whether **previous reasoning content is preserved across agent/tool turns differently from the official Z.AI implementation**.

If an abnormal reasoning sequence is fed back into subsequent turns, it may potentially explain why a long-running agent session can enter a persistent non-progressing reasoning state.

---

## Environment

### Ollama Cloud

- Subscription: **Ollama Pro**
- Service: **Ollama Cloud API at ollama.com**
- Model: **`glm-5.3:cloud`**
- Local Ollama daemon: **No**
- Local Ollama model: **No**
- Direct Cloud API access: **Yes**

### OpenCode

- OpenCode version: v1.18.20
- Oh My OpenCode installed: **Yes**
- Provider: **Ollama Cloud API**
- Model: `glm-5.3:cloud`
- Result: endless reasoning / task abort can occur

Control:

- Provider: **official Z.AI API**
- Model: GLM-5.3
- Result: works normally

### ZCode

- ZCode version: the last
- Provider: **Ollama Cloud API**
- Model: `glm-5.3:cloud`
- Result: endless reasoning / task abort can occur

Control:

- Provider: **official Z.AI API**
- Model: GLM-5.3

---

## Additional information I can provide

If useful, I can provide:

- OpenCode logs from a failed run;
- ZCode logs from a failed run;
- screenshots showing the model stuck in reasoning;
- a representative coding task that triggered the issue;
- timestamps of failed Ollama Cloud requests;

If there is a recommended method for capturing the **raw Ollama Cloud API request/response stream**, especially:

- reasoning fields;

items.title: qwen3 tool call parser returns 500 when model output is truncated
items.body:
## Summary

When using Qwen3 models with tool calling, if the model's generated tool call JSON is truncated (due to hitting `num_predict` or context window limits), `qwen3.go:108` fails to parse the incomplete JSON and returns an HTTP 500 instead of gracefully handling the situation.

This makes Qwen3 tool calling unreliable for tasks that produce large tool call arguments (e.g., writing files with substantial content).

## Behavior

**Expected:** When the model's output is truncated mid-tool-call, Ollama should either:
1. Return the generated text as regular `content` (not as a tool call), or
2. Return a response with `done_reason: "length"` so the client can handle it

**Actual:** Ollama returns HTTP 500 with no usable response. The server log shows:

```
level=WARN source=qwen3.go:108 msg="qwen3 tool call parsing failed" error="failed to parse JSON: unexpected end of JSON input"
[GIN] | 500 | 1m35s | 127.0.0.1 | POST "/api/chat"
```

## Reproduction

1. Use any Qwen3 model with tools enabled
2. Send a prompt that causes the model to emit a tool call with a very large argument (e.g., "write a complete HTML game to a file" where the file content is a tool call argument)
3. Use default `num_predict` (or set it low enough that the tool call JSON gets truncated)

The model generates 1-3 minutes of output, hits the token limit, and the incomplete JSON fails parsing.

**With `num_predict: -1`:** Most calls succeed (200), but if the conversation history + generation fills the context window, the same truncation/500 occurs.

### Minimal repro

```bash
curl http://localhost:11434/api/chat -d '{
  "model": "qwen3.5:35b-a3b",
  "stream": false,
  "options": {"num_predict": 200},
  "tools": [{
    "type": "function",
    "function": {
      "name": "write_file",
      "description": "Write content to a file",
      "parameters": {
        "type": "object",
        "properties": {
          "path": {"type": "string"},
          "content": {"type": "string"}
        },
        "required": ["path", "content"]
      }
    }
  }],
  "messages": [
    {"role": "user", "content": "Write a 500-line Python web server to /tmp/server.py"}
  ]
}'
```

With `num_predict: 200`, the model will attempt a `write_file` tool call but the JSON will be truncated, resulting in a 500.

## Log excerpt

Over a ~20 minute window with repeated retries on the same prompt:

```
19:16:02 level=WARN source=qwen3.go:108 msg="qwen3 tool call parsing failed" error="failed to parse JSON: unexpected end of JSON input"
19:16:02 [GIN] | 500 | 43.17s | POST "/api/chat"
19:20:08 level=WARN source=qwen3.go:108 msg="qwen3 tool call parsing failed" error="failed to parse JSON: unexpected end of JSON input"
19:20:08 [GIN] | 500 | 1m47s | POST "/api/chat"
19:21:47 level=WARN source=qwen3.go:108 msg="qwen3 tool call parsing failed" error="failed to parse JSON: unexpected end of JSON input"
19:21:47 [GIN] | 500 | 1m38s | POST "/api/chat"
(repeated ~12 more times, every ~1.5 min)
```

After setting `num_predict: -1`, most calls succeed but the 500 still occurs when context window fills:

```
19:48:52 level=WARN source=qwen3.go:108 msg="qwen3 tool call parsing failed" error="failed to parse JSON: unexpected end of JSON input"
19:48:52 [GIN] | 500 | 1m15s | POST "/api/chat"
```

## Environment

- **Ollama version:** 0.17.4
- **Model:** qwen3.5:35b-a3b
- **OS:** Ubuntu 24.04.3 LTS, kernel 6.17.0-14-generic
- **GPU:** 3x NVIDIA (RTX 3090 Ti 24GB + RTX 3090 24GB + RTX 3060 12GB)
- **num_ctx:** 60000
- **stream:** false
